text: 🇲🇽📋 Daily — Sábado 6 de junio de 2026 Sheinbaum está en gira por Veracruz hoy (Xalapa: Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro; Martínez de la Torre: obras de protección contra inundaciones del río Bobos). Las versiones estenográficas aún no se publican en gob.mx. La corrida de las 8 PM debería alcanzar los eventos del día.

🇲🇽🌎 CONSUMER CONFIDENCE DIPS TO 43.5 — TARIFFS AND GLOBAL INSTABILITY HITTING SENTIMENT WORLDWIDE

INEGI: Mexico's Consumer Confidence Index fell 0.7 points in May to 43.5, a 41-month low. All five components declined — expectations for the country's economy over the next 12 months dropped the most at 1.6 points.

For context: US Michigan consumer sentiment hit 44.8 in May — its lowest since 1952, a 74-year record. Both economies absorbing the damage from tariffs and the Iran war's oil shock.

Mexico's fundamentals tell a different story: labor poverty at a 21-year low of 30.7%, wages up 152% since 2018, unemployment at 2.5%.

🚨🇨🇴 COLOMBIA'S NATIONAL TEAM HARASSED AFTER FLAG CEREMONY WITH PETRO

The Colombian Football Federation denounced "harassment" against World Cup players after edited videos circulated showing them allegedly snubbing President Petro at the official flag ceremony in Bogotá.

Coach Néstor Lorenzo: "misinterpretations" and "edited videos" — the team is "100% committed to the Colombian shirt and flag for everyone, for all 50 million inhabitants."

The manufactured controversy arrives as Colombia heads to its June 21 presidential runoff — Petro ally Iván Cepeda vs. far-right Abelardo de la Espriella. Sports weaponized for electoral gain.

🇲🇽🌽 30 YEARS OF NAFTA DEVASTATED MEXICAN AGRICULTURE — CORN IMPORTS UP 9,000%

In 1993, Mexico imported 286,000 tons of US corn. By 2025: 26.1 million tons — a 9,000% increase. US corn sales to Mexico went from $35 million to nearly $6 billion.

Cultivated corn land shrank from 9.2 million hectares to 6.9 million — a 24% collapse. One of every two kilos of corn consumed domestically now comes from the United States.

With the TMEC review starting June 16, farmers are mobilizing nationwide to demand corn, wheat, and rice be excluded from the agreement.

🇲🇽⚽ MEXICO DEPLOYS MASSIVE INFRASTRUCTURE FOR WORLD CUP — 30,000 CAMERAS, 500 REBUILT FIELDS

CDMX alone: 30,000 new surveillance cameras, 185,000 light fixtures, 334 km of Safe Routes for Women, and 3,500 additional patrol units.

Nationwide: 500 reconstructed soccer fields, 30 free football festivals, Zócalo broadcast transmissions, and the transformation of Calzada de Tlalpan with bike lanes and elevated parks.

Brugada's directive: events must be "free from discrimination, homophobia, racism, and violence."

🚨🇸🇻 700 SALVADORANS MARCH AGAINST BUKELE'S MINING REVIVAL ON WORLD ENVIRONMENT DAY

In December 2024, Bukele repealed El Salvador's total ban on mineral extraction — enacted in 2017, the first such ban in the world.

His argument: it's "absurd" to prohibit mining when El Salvador has "the highest gold density per square kilometer in the world."

Environmental groups estimate mining exploitation would affect 4 million people across seven northern departments. Polls from 2007, 2015, and 2024 all show over 60% of Salvadorans oppose mining to protect their water sources.

🚨🇨🇺 US SIEGE BLEEDS CUBA'S TOURISM DRY — HOTEL CHAINS FLEE, AIRLINES CANCEL

Blue Diamond pulled out of 62 hotels. Meliá dropped 15 more. Iberostar left 12. Archipelago International gone. Air Canada suspended Cuba flights indefinitely — and Canada used to send 40% of the island's tourists.

Tourism revenue projections collapsed from $1.8 billion to $400-600 million. Up to one million fewer visitors expected.

Trump's January 29 executive order authorized punitive tariffs against any country that supplies oil to Cuba. That's not "democracy promotion" — it's economic strangulation of 11 million people.
